design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — utility_line_repairs task 0 (interior slab-leak recall, over-cap reroute).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed: {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 4]}. The tree has one prerequisite problem; lineplan_ext_slab_access_payment and lineplan_ext_interior_work_payment take 4 factors each. Task 1's draw ([5, 5, 6], two prerequisite problems) is served by the exterior tree it claims.

[Scope snapshot] First task. Claimed here: lineplan_ext_slab_access_payment (tool authorize_slab_access_payment_bcc8b3fe, owner agent) and lineplan_ext_interior_work_payment (tool approve_interior_line_work_4d5cfcfa, owner user). Left for task 1: the public-way and lawn restoration allowances and the exterior over-cap approval, each a separate policy and tool. No cancellation/credit/refund policy exists in the charter: the base cancellation credit nets all benefit paid in the term against a premium of a few hundred dollars and floors at zero, so repair activity would make its factors bear no weight.

[Revision record — rework round 2 after the policy-task audit]
 * F-1 / T0-1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED): symptom — slab_household_alignment and interior_household_extension raised line-plan payments by the tier or limits of a separate HomeCare contract; root cause — a line protection program does not weigh another product's tier for a slab-access allowance or a line payment, and the charter's own coordination rule makes the line plan the primary payer on its own terms. Change — both factors removed; the slab policy now rests on slab_recall_offset, slab_opening_rate (drain line, or supply line under an attached home whose slab is shared), slab_cutting_addition (emergency with same-day or next-day first assignment) and slab_partner_schedule (partner-program schedule while the plan is billed through that partner); the interior policy's cross-difficulty factor is interior_wall_restoration, which sizes the drywall restored after a reroute by the living area recorded on the household's homeowner service contract (a cost driver of a reroute, read from another difficulty's record). slab_tenure_addition (loyalty, O-1) was also removed. World changed accordingly: plan enrolled through Prairie Gas and Light and billed on its bill (6 billing rows added), property recorded as a townhome on both contracts, HomeCare row no longer carries a mid-term upgrade, June dispatch dated the day after its request, June slab entry 790.00 (the rule at its own date), quote $4,980. Re-run results below.
 * T0-2 (SOURCE-CHAIN RED): the closure and this dossier claimed the recall request's only claim event was its determination; the recall dispatch f3a0f9ec-397a-400c-8ab6-c2ef8cbb2e93 also sits on it. Both texts now list the two events and state the true ground (no slab access allowance on the recall request).
 * O-3/O-5: every rule now says the payment is figured on the day it is booked from the records as they then stand, with periods 'to the request date' ending on the request date, and month windows run back from the booking day — the same anchor the computation uses.
 * O-4: the allowance's open-benefit limit now deducts the continuation request as well as the recalled request, the same occurrence the permanent-work scope uses.
[Revision record — rework round 3 after the lineplan render notes and the round-2 observations]
 * Render item 2 (living-area unit): the wall-restoration and material-upgrade rules now say the large-home and upsizing areas are in square feet, the unit of the living area recorded on the homeowner service contract.
 * Render item 3 (recovery share): the workmanship recovery is now the share of the payment on the authorization that the recalled completion closed, where that authorization is a section repair; a completed authorization is never reversed (base), so no netting question arises. The computation reads that one authorization through the completion's authorization number instead of summing every section repair on the request; the figure on this world is unchanged because that request carries a single section repair.
 * Render item 1 (scope vs cap branches): each allowance and exterior rule now states its cap line by line, and the public-way computation no longer carries a septic branch the public-way scope never named. No value on this world moves.
 * O-8: the next-day emergency cutting tier now has its own rationale sentence. O-9: the size-tier rules state why a home with no living area on Bridgewell's records takes the standard size. O-10: the cold-weather, lawn-season and frost-excavation ladders were bound to a territory (round 3 used a ZIP first-digit test, replaced in round 4 by the frost territory of states with a design frost depth of at least 36 inches). O-11: the sewer commissioning contribution is named as the acceptance camera inspection and declared against the base camera-inside-cap sentence with a scoped replaced_by. O-12: the wall-restoration rationale states that drywall is not one of the base restoration allowances. task_tools.py is unchanged.
 Re-run: every task-0 figure, sensitivity and fall-back recomputes unchanged; gates re-run green (see the gate results below).
[Revision record — rework round 4 after the policy re-audit, revision 3]
 * R3-F1 / R3-T1-1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED): the round-3 frost-zone test (first digit of the ZIP code) was a postal region, not a frost territory, and its stated basis was inverted. The three seasonal ladders (public-way cold-weather addition, lawn season rate, exterior frost excavation) now use the frost territory: the states whose plumbing code sets a design frost depth of at least 36 inches for buried water lines across most of the state — Alaska, Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois, Iowa, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New York, North Dakota, Rhode Island, South Dakota, Vermont, Wisconsin and Wyoming — because there the soil over a service line freezes deep enough that winter excavation must break frozen ground. The rules read the state from the first three digits of the plan's recorded ZIP code (005, 010-069, 100-149, 480-629, 680-693, 800-831, 995-999 exactly cover those states' ZIP-3 ranges), and the computations test the same ranges. Every tier stays reachable. Task 0 has no seasonal factor; nothing in its tree moves.

[Why this is a good test] The customer only asks what Bridgewell pays toward a $4,980 reroute and wants to approve it. The agent must (1) read from the interior permanent-work rule that its result waits on the service request carrying its slab access entry, see in the claim history that the recall request has none, and work out that the slab access policy's write brings it about; (2) compute that payment from four factors over the request, its dispatch, the plan's billing history and the June occurrence; (3) recompute the interior payment after that write, reconciling the June occurrence because the request is a recall, restoring half the June repair under the workmanship recovery, adding the reroute contribution and the wall restoration sized from the household's homeowner service contract (another difficulty's record); (4) hand the approval to the customer because over-cap work is her own decision.

[Problem-tree card] root lineplan_ext_interior_work_payment; prerequisite lineplan_ext_slab_access_payment; edge value_input, gate i_this_net, form state. Prerequisite sentence (affirmative): "For an interior line that lies beneath a concrete slab or foundation, the interior permanent-work payment is fixed only after the service request carries its slab access entry." Four-point test: connective 'only after'; waits on a record-visible state (an allowance of type slab access on the request); names no tool, id or code token; hard requirement scoped to interior lines beneath a slab. Exactly one write of this difficulty books slab access entries (authorize_slab_access_payment_bcc8b3fe). Opening evidence: the recall request 5e96c423-4d8f-4052-a611-da610f330166 carries its recall dispatch f3a0f9ec-397a-400c-8ab6-c2ef8cbb2e93 and its covered determination 5ecc8520-2dec-4a3c-add5-13ca22134e61, and no slab access entry; the one slab access entry, 17acfa7e-1f29-4bbd-866e-b8bd332043f7, is on the June request. Derivation: sentence + claim history + the slab rule ('booked as one allowance authorization of type slab access') -> the slab access write. Order [lineplan_ext_slab_access_payment, lineplan_ext_interior_work_payment]. Deletion run: skipping the slab write gives 2,240.00 instead of 2,140.00.

[Factor card — lineplan_ext_slab_access_payment] baseline: flat 500.00, limited by the open interior benefit, rounded once; fall-back here 500.00.
 * slab_recall_offset (method): figure less slab access already on the recalled request / on a continuation's temporary-repair request / in full. Taken: recall (99 days after 2026-06-09): 890.00 - 790.00 = 100.00. Baseline 570.00.
 * slab_opening_rate (parameter): drain 1.4 / supply line of a townhome or duplex 1.2 / 1.0. Taken: 1.2 (supply line; property recorded as a townhome). Baseline 0.00.
 * slab_cutting_addition (parameter, multi-source): emergency with first assignment on the request date 200.00 / emergency with a later first assignment 100.00 / 0. Taken: same-day (recall dispatched 2026-09-16, its request date). Baseline 0.00. Near-miss: the June request's first assignment came the next day.
 * slab_partner_schedule (parameter, multi-source): Prairie Gas and Light 1.15 / Tri-County Electric Cooperative 1.1 / 1.0, each while the premium was remitted through that utility's bill within 12 months. Taken: Prairie (2026-09-01 remittance; the 2025-09-02 one is 12 whole months back, outside — near-miss). Baseline 10.00.
[Factor card — lineplan_ext_interior_work_payment] baseline: 3,000.00 interior cap less this request's own net amounts; fall-back here 2,900.00.
 * interior_occurrence_scope (method): taken recall: deduct 100.00 + 2,430.00; baseline 4,570.00.
 * interior_workmanship_recovery (parameter): full 1.0 (<= 90 days) / half 0.5 (91-180) / 0; taken half (99 days) of 1,640.00; baseline 1,320.00. The June slab entry is not a section repair payment and is not restored.
 * interior_reroute_contribution (parameter): drain 600.00 / supply 400.00 under whole-line work / 0; taken supply; baseline 1,740.00.
 * interior_wall_restoration (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty homeplan): large-home 450.00 (recorded living area >= 2,000) / standard 300.00 (below, or none recorded) / 0, under whole-line work; taken large-home (2,240 sq ft on 5539fdb9-842f-4616-b8d7-2ea281214c4d); baseline 1,690.00; cross-category reads off -> 1,990.00.
 The quote 4,980.00 stays above every fall-back figure (largest 4,570.00), so the work is over-cap on every reading. Base departures are declared in overwrite with scoped replaced_by sentences.

[Base-invariant card] Both writes are lineplan_repair_authorization rows governed only by lineplan_evt_repair_authorization; its eligibility line_covered_before_work ('Line work is authorized only after a covered determination is on file for the service request.') holds through the covered determination 5ecc8520-2dec-4a3c-add5-13ca22134e61 on 5e96c423-4d8f-4052-a611-da610f330166, bound to the argument lineplan_service_request_id. No time gate (temporal_feasibility = []). The base recall rule is honoured by the occurrence scope and the offset; the base whole-line rule (break count 2, a completed repair 99 days earlier, within 730) makes the reroute a full_line_replacement.

[Business-object card] Target: recall request 5e96c423-4d8f-4052-a611-da610f330166 on plan 58b5227f-5b0d-4f26-ab48-a29f48625bdc. Included: the recall request's own authorizations (none at opening; the slab entry after step 9) and, as the recalled occurrence, the June request 5debfd92-52e6-4a76-8202-6e16065628a0 (slab access 58632422 790.00, section repair 56088848 1,640.00, completion e486bfb3-ac6b-49d7-bc0e-eaf48e8d7679). No reversals exist; no temporary repair exists anywhere on the plan.

[World rows] customers 1; lineplan_contracts 1; lineplan_service_requests 2; lineplan_claim_events 7 (June: dispatch, determination, slab 790.00, section repair 1,640.00, completion; recall: dispatch, determination); lineplan_billing_entries 6 (annual premiums 2024-2026 and their Prairie Gas and Light remittances); homeplan_contracts 1 (Gold, townhome, 2,240 sq ft — the cross-difficulty evidence); service_contractors 1 (FK parent of both dispatches). Each historical entry equals its own policy at its own booking date (seed_consistency). Automatic clauses: premium paid, no suspension, no renewal pending, HomeCare active with zero balance.

[Persona design] Marisol, a retired librarian, warm but to the point; volunteers the leak, the reopened floor, the $4,980 reroute quote, wants approval today and will pay the difference. Only when asked: phone and email, the quote line, supply line not drain, same plumber, home warranty on the townhome, line plan billed on her Prairie Gas and Light bill. Passive: agrees to a claim entry first only if told; approves when handed the tool with the figures read to her; asks for a re-check only on self-contradicting figures; ends at the approval confirmation.

[Verification run] python3 /tmp/utility_lines_0058/t0_calc.py: slab payment 100.00 (sensitivities slab_recall_offset=570.00, slab_opening_rate=0.00, slab_cutting_addition=0.00, slab_partner_schedule=10.00; all-baseline 500.00); interior payment 2,140.00 (sensitivities interior_occurrence_scope=4,570.00, interior_workmanship_recovery=1,320.00, interior_reroute_contribution=1,740.00, interior_wall_restoration=1,690.00; all-baseline 2,900.00); skip-slab interior payment 2,240.00; cross reads off 1,990.00.
[Gate results — rework round 4, per-task (--task N) and difficulty-wide runs from the repository root with .venv/bin/python] check_extended: EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools: TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK (task_tools.py byte-identical since round 1); replay_tasks: REPLAY OK (task 0: 12 actions, closure 19 = initial 19; task 1: 14 actions, closure 32 = initial 32; deterministic, non-vacuous, no errors); check_solvability: SOLVABILITY OK (task 0: 2 calls, 2 base gates, 16 seed rows; task 1: 3 calls, 3 base gates, 29 seed rows); check_compute: COMPUTE OK (task 0: 2 computations, 8 factors, 1 cross-difficulty, 13 history rows, 27 branches; task 1: 3 computations, 16 factors, 1 cross-difficulty, 36 history rows, 63 branches; suite means branches 45.00 / steps 13.00, history max 36, branch max 63); check_grounding: GROUNDING OK; check_traceability: TRACEABILITY OK (task 0: 22 copied, 0 missing; task 1: 28 copied, 0 missing — the published KB now carries the hidden tool names); check_cross_fire: SCOPE OK; check_cache_diff: informational only (no cache trap chosen).

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Interior rule -> payment waits on the slab access entry (absent on the recall request). Slab: 500 x 1.2 (supply line, townhome) x 1.15 (Prairie, remitted 2026-09-01) + 200 (emergency, dispatched the request day) = 890, recall offset -790 = 100, open benefit 570 -> book 100 on the recall request. Interior: 3,000 - (100 + 790 + 1,640) = 470, + 820 (half of 1,640, 99 days) + 400 (supply reroute) + 450 (2,240 sq ft recorded) = 2,140 < 4,980 -> customer approves full_line_replacement / not_applicable / 4,980 / 2,140. Agrees with gold.

[Closure] lineplan_ext_slab_access_payment -> authorize_slab_access_payment_bcc8b3fe -> computations[0] step 9 payment_amount; lineplan_ext_interior_work_payment -> approve_interior_line_work_4d5cfcfa -> computations[1] step 11 bridgewell_payment. charter_scope and required_documents = [lineplan_ext_slab_access_payment, lineplan_ext_interior_work_payment]. No handoff; no state_due obligation lit.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Quintanilla-Hartwell, a retired middle-school librarian who owns and lives in the townhome at 1843 East Saguaro Ridge Court in Chandler, Arizona. You are warm and chatty by nature, but today you are tired of wet tile and you get to the point. You are calling Bridgewell because the leak under your family room floor is back. In June a Bridgewell plumber found a broken water pipe under the concrete slab, patched it and closed the floor up again. This week the same spot was wet again and the water meter was spinning, so you called it in and the plumber came back out. He had to break open the floor again to find it, and this time he says patching it is pointless: the pipe has to be rerouted through the attic, and his written quote for that is $4,980. You open by explaining all of that and saying you want to know what Bridgewell will pay toward the reroute and you want the work approved today so he can start; the plumber warned you it might not all be covered, and you are ready to approve it yourself and pay him the difference if that is how it works.

You keep the plumber's quote sheet in front of you. If the representative asks what the quote is for, you read it out: "Reroute cold water supply line through attic, abandon line under slab, $4,980." That is the only line on the sheet; you do not have any other figures from him and you do not know what anything else costs. If asked whether he is the same plumber who did the June repair, you say yes, the same man from the same company. If asked about the leak, it is the water line to the house under the family room slab, not a drain; water was coming up through the grout.

You do not remember your plan number or customer number and ask the representative to look you up. When asked to identify yourself you give your phone number, 4805550186, and when asked for one more detail you give your email address, marisol.quintanilla.hartwell@saguaromail.net. If asked which coverage you have, you only know it is the Bridgewell plan for all the water, sewer and other lines at the townhome, and that you also have a Bridgewell home warranty on the townhome; if asked how you pay for the line plan, it comes once a year on your Prairie Gas and Light bill. You leave the details to the representative's records.

If the representative tells you something has to be recorded on the claim before the payment can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead. Once the representative tells you how much Bridgewell will pay and how much you would owe the plumber, you sigh that it is more than you hoped, but you say you want it done and you will approve it. When the representative hands the approval over to you, you complete it yourself using exactly the reference numbers, the kind of work, the method and the amounts the representative reads out to you, together with the $4,980 from your quote sheet, and you read back the confirmation it gives you. If the representative tells you a figure that does not match what they told you a moment earlier, you ask them to check it against the record before you approve anything. Once the approval confirmation comes back, you thank the representative and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.bridgewell_payment: 2,140.00 — interior occurrence scope: a recall within the 180-day guarantee, so the 3,000.00 cap is reduced by the recall request's net 100.00 (the slab access booked at step 9) and the June request's net 2,430.00 (790.00 + 1,640.00) = 470.00 left open; interior workmanship recovery: recall reported 99 days after completion (> 90 full recovery days, <= 180) so the half share 0.5 x the 1,640.00 section repair authorization 56088848 that the June completion closed = 820.00; whole-line work: break count 2 > 0 and the latest completed repair (2026-06-09) is within 730 days of 2026-09-16; interior reroute contribution for a supply line = 400.00; interior wall restoration: living area 2240 square feet recorded on the active HomeCare contract for the same address, at least the 2,000 large-home area = 450.00; payment = 470.00 + 820.00 + 400.00 + 450.00 = 2,140.00, below the 4,980.00 quote so the customer pays 2,840.00.

slab_opening_rate (parameter): line_type interior_supply_line on a plan whose property_type is townhome -> attached-home rate 1.2; baseline 1.0 gives 0.00.

Near-miss: the June request's first assignment was the day after its request (next-day tier), which is why the June slab entry was smaller.

slab_partner_schedule (parameter, multi-source): partner Prairie Gas and Light AND utility_bill remittance 275.89 on 2026-09-01 within 12 months (the 2025-09-02 and 2024-09-03 remittances are outside) -> 1.15; baseline 1.0 gives 10.00.

non-factor bindings: request = latest request 5e96c423-4d8f-4052-a611-da610f330166 (2026-09-16); figure = 500.00 x 1.2 x 1.15 + 200.00 = 890.00; occurrence benefit still open = 3,000.00 - 0.00 - 2,430.00 = 570.00; result = min(100.00, 570.00) rounded = 100.00.

edges.condition: The service request of an interior line beneath a slab carries an allowance authorization of type slab access in the plan's claim history, not reversed.
edges.policy_source: For an interior line that lies beneath a concrete slab or foundation, the interior permanent-work payment is fixed only after the service request carries its slab access entry.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time the recall request carries two claim events, its recall dispatch (f3a0f9ec-397a-400c-8ab6-c2ef8cbb2e93) and its covered determination (5ecc8520-2dec-4a3c-add5-13ca22134e61), and no allowance authorization of type slab access; the only slab access entry in the history (17acfa7e-1f29-4bbd-866e-b8bd332043f7) belongs to the June request, although the plumber opened the slab again on the recall.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 9 books a lineplan_repair_authorization with allowance_type slab_access and amount 100.00 on request 5e96c423-4d8f-4052-a611-da610f330166; the recall request's net authorized amount (i_this_net) goes from 0.00 to 100.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: One prerequisite edge only (no parallel prerequisites); the order slab access entry -> interior approval is the order the prerequisite sentence states, and the reverse order changes the scored payment (see edge_load_bearing).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the slab access write and replaying the rest leaves i_this_net at 0.00, so the interior permanent-work payment recomputes to 2,240.00 instead of 2,140.00, and the terminal claim history lacks the slab access authorization.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions an allowance, an entry for the floor opening, or anything to be settled first; it describes the leak, the floor the plumber opened, the reroute quote and the wish to approve the work. The only reference to recording something first is a passive reaction ('If the representative tells you something has to be recorded on the claim before the payment can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead'), triggered only by the agent.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: approve_interior_line_work_4d5cfcfa in task_tools.py performs one ctx.create of the authorization with the arguments given; it reads no other row, checks no slab access entry and returns no error, so it would book a payment even with the prerequisite unmet. authorize_slab_access_payment_bcc8b3fe likewise creates its allowance row unconditionally.
